title: Imported-car air conditioning: check serviceability
meta_description: Before buying abroad, identify the actual refrigerant label, compressor-oil specification and a qualified destination workshop. Cold air alone is not enough.
h1: Buying a car abroad: check whether its air conditioning can be serviced at home
author: AutoBridge Export Editorial Team
image_alt: Three-panel editorial diagram showing three purchasing questions from the article.
image_caption: Original editorial diagram, not a photograph of a vehicle or an inspection.
summary: A seller sends a video: the dashboard is lit, the fan is running and someone says the air is cold. It may be a useful demonstration of operation at that moment. It does not identify the refrigerant, establish which compressor oil belongs in the system or show that a workshop at your destination can service the car correctly. For an overseas purchase, those unanswered questions can matter as much as the demonstration itself.
